subject: Peripheral nervous system
hook: PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Despite being cranial nerves, the olfactory (CN I) and optic (CN II) nerves are not part of the peripheral nervous system but belong to the central nervous system
angle_support: "In the somatic nervous system, the cranial nerves are part of the PNS with the exceptions of the olfactory nerve and ... the optic nerve (cranial nerve II) ... considered parts of the central nervous system"
"The second cranial nerve is not a true peripheral nerve but a tract of the diencephalon"
title: Why Smell and Vision Aren’t Peripheral Nerves
description: Most people think the smell and sight nerves are just like other cranial nerves that leave the brain. In reality, they develop from brain tissue and stay within the central nervous system.
narration: PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You assume the olfactory (CN I) and optic (CN II) nerves are peripheral cranial nerves. Actually, they are direct extensions of the brain, belonging to the central nervous system. Embryologically, CN I and CN II arise from the forebrain, lack peripheral ganglia, and are classified as central tracts in the adult anatomy and the optic nerve is a diencephalic fiber bundle, not a true peripheral nerve. Those two senses travel inside the brain, not outside of you.
